version.changelog: Balance and cost questions now answer from a live account read rather than from figures written into the package.

llm.summary: The skill does the advertised voice-clip work, but it also requests broad Beatra account authority and silently updates its own code, so it needs Review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The package records platform, hostname-derived device name, package version, and a stable installation reference for authorization and registration; this is disclosed but exceeds the minimum needed to generate audio clips.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation and authentication are disclosed and use private local files under ~/.beatra, but the bundled client silently checks for and installs remote package updates by default before ordinary commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The Skill gives clear user-confirmation gates for paid clone and speech work, but scripts/mcp_client.py exposes an arbitrary MCP tool-name proxy with the shared bearer token instead of enforcing a package-specific allowlist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a shared device token, installation inventory, registration cache, host metadata, and update state under ~/.beatra, and uninstall.py can revoke and remove shared Beatra state when it believes this is the last installed Beatra skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The voice workflow is coherent and requires speech, voice, upload, task, and billing operations, but authorize.py requests unrelated image, video, music, wallet spending, artifact read, task cancel, and generic MCP tool scopes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting this package a shared, broad Beatra device authorization and allowing default silent package updates. Consider disabling automatic updates with the documented command, reviewing the Beatra approval permissions, and revoking the device from the Beatra Console if you no longer want the connection.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Lifecycle management is disclosed in the Skill references and uninstall.py is conservative, but bundling shared credential revocation and cleanup into a voice skill contributes to Review-level privilege concerns.
[AE1] expected: The referenced bundled client was locally available and inspected; the references to scripts/mcp_client.py are not evidence of analysis evasion in this workspace.
[PE3] expected: Credential-file access is expected for the declared device-bearer Beatra integration and is accompanied by permission checks and warnings not to print tokens, but the credential is broad and shared.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The requested OAuth scope set is broader than a shift-handoff voice workflow needs, including unrelated media generation, wallet spending, artifact reading, and task cancellation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The self-update path downloads and replaces package-owned executable files without separate confirmation; the checksum and path controls reduce tampering risk but do not remove the post-review code-change concern.
[RA1] unexpected: The update command and default silent updater create persistent package self-modification capability that is not necessary for generating the requested voice clips.
[SDI-2] unexpected: uninstall.py can delete shared ~/.beatra state files after inventory checks; the behavior is disclosed and guarded, but it affects state beyond this single skill's package directory.
[T05] unexpected: Static-scan concerns about broad authorization and unrestricted MCP proxy are supported by authorize.py and mcp_client.py and are material to the Review verdict.
[T03] unexpected: Static-scan concerns about mutable remote code installation are supported by the default-on maybe_auto_update flow in mcp_client.py.
[other] unexpected: Hostname, platform, and stable installation telemetry are limited and disclosed, so this is a privacy note rather than an independent malicious signal.
